title: EAT IT ON THE SAME DAY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The meat of their fellowship offering of thanksgiving must be eaten on the day it is offered; they must leave none of it till morning.'" - Lev 7:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Eat it today. Keep nothing back for tomorrow.

Practically, this was sensible in a hot climate without refrigeration. But it also had an effect on the worshipper: he could not eat this meal alone. A whole animal, consumed in one day, meant inviting people. Family, neighbours, the poor, the Levite.

God designed thanksgiving so that it spilled over onto other people.

That is still how gratitude works best. Kept private, it fades quickly. Shared — spoken aloud, turned into hospitality, turned into generosity — it multiplies and encourages everyone who hears it.

There is also a lesson about not hoarding what God gives. Israel learned this with manna, which bred worms when kept overnight (Ex 16:20). God repeatedly trained His people to receive daily and trust Him for tomorrow. Jesus taught us to pray for daily bread (Mtt 6:11) and not to worry about tomorrow (Mtt 6:34).

Something in us wants to store up God's blessings rather than use them. But grace is not preserved by hoarding. It is enjoyed by spending.

If God has been good to you lately, do not keep it till morning. Tell someone. Feed someone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I keep God's blessings to myself rather than sharing them?
2. Who could I invite in — practically or in conversation — to share what God has done for me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for Your goodness to me. Help me to spend it on others today rather than storing it up. Amen.
